newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TNT recommends KPN takeover bid.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TNT recommends KPN takeover bid.

text.p: Transport group TNT Ltd said on Wednesday it had agreed to a A$2.45 per share cash takeover offer it had received from Dutch Telecom group Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN).

The bid values TNT at A$2.0 billion. "The boards of ... KPN, the primary postal and telecommunications corporation of the Netherlands, and TNT Ltd, the worldwide transport and logistics group based in Australia, announce that they have unanimously agreed recommended cash offers made by KPN for all of the shares of TNT," they said in a joint statement.

"The directors of TNT unanimously recommend that shareholders in TNT accept KPN's offer, in the absence of a superior offer, as they intend to do in respect of all of their own shares and share options," TNT said in the statement.
The agreement followed long strategic discussions between KPN and TNT about the benefits of combining TNT's businesses with KPN's postal subsidiary, TNT and KPN said.
"It will create a new global force in the time sensitive distribution and logistics industry, ranking in the top four world-wide," they said.
TNT's share price closed up two cents at A$1.63 on Tuesday.
"This proposal represents an outstanding opportunity to create a strong global transportation group," TNT managing director David Mortimer said.
"For TNT shareholders, it delivers premium value," he said.
KPN chairman and chief executive Wim Dik said the acquisition was a significant step in the company's growth strategy.
